::: {.lead}
Today you give four jobs to an AI assistant, you put the results into
Word, and you check every answer. Each experiment has two parts. **Part
A** is in the AI assistant and Word on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word, a browser and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com` with your
  university account).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Word.
- **Never type personal data** into an AI tool: the start file has only
  made-up details.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · A first draft

**The idea:** AI writes a **first draft** fast: a notice, an e-mail, a
letter. You give the facts in the prompt, then you read every line: the AI
can add facts that nobody gave, and you delete them. Paste into Word with
**Keep Text Only**, so that the styles of Word give the look.

**Aim:** let the AI write a first draft, then keep only your facts.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. In the AI assistant, type this prompt: *Write a short notice for the
   staff of a small office. The printer on the first floor is broken.
   Please use the printer on the second floor until Tuesday. Three short
   lines.* Read every line. Find every fact that you did **not** give.

   {{< record "The first line … ; facts that I did not give (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good draft has your three facts: the printer on the **first floor** is
   broken, use the printer on the **second floor**, until **Tuesday**. The
   AI often adds something, for example "A technician comes on Monday" or
   "Call IT on 123": nobody said it, so you delete it.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   A draft has five lines. Keep or delete? Sort them.

   Your fact: keep it
   :   The printer on the first floor is broken.

       Why: You gave this fact.

   :   Please use the printer on the second floor.

       Why: You gave this fact.

   :   You can use it until Tuesday.

       Why: Tuesday is in your prompt.

   Not given: delete it
   :   A technician comes on Monday.

       Why: Nobody said it: the AI invented it.

   :   Call IT on 123.

       Why: A phone number that nobody gave: delete it.
   :::

2. Copy the draft. Open a new Word document and paste it with **Keep Text
   Only** (right-click › Paste Options › the button with the letter A).
   Give the first line the style **Title**, and save the file as
   `printer-notice.docx`.

   {{< record "Why Keep Text Only?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Keep Text Only** pastes only the words, without the look of the chat.
   Then the styles of Word give the look: the first line is a Title.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Why paste with **Keep Text Only**?

   - [x] It pastes only the words, without the look of the chat.

     Why: Then the styles of Word give the look.

   - [ ] It pastes the words and the colours of the chat.

     Why: That is Keep Source Formatting.

   - [ ] It deletes the facts that the AI added.

     Why: Only you can find and delete them.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.png" title="Word AI Lab: draft, sum up, rewrite, translate" >}}

3. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Draft**. Compare the e-mail with the memo
   and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong part, and the right fact" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   "Our shop will also close at 1 pm on that day": the memo says the
   **shop stays open until 6 pm**. The AI added a wrong fact, so you fix
   it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The draft says: "Our shop will also close at 1 pm on that day." What
   does the memo say?

   - [x] The shop stays open until 6 pm: only the office closes early.

     Why: The AI added a wrong fact; the memo is the source.

   - [ ] The shop closes at 1 pm too.

     Why: That is the AI's sentence, not the memo.

   - [ ] Nothing about the shop.

     Why: The memo says the shop stays open until 6 pm.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A summary

**The idea:** a **summary** keeps the main points of a long text. AI sums up
fast, but it can change a number, and it always drops details. Check every
point with the original: each day, time, number and name. Add a dropped
detail again if your reader needs it.

**Aim:** let the AI sum up a report, and check every point with the report.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Word and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Open `report-start.docx` (click **Enable Editing** if you see it). Press
   **Ctrl + A** and **Ctrl + C**. In the AI assistant, type *Sum up this
   report in 3 short points:* and paste the report. Compare each point with
   the report: the day, the time, the numbers and the names.

   {{< record "The 3 points … ; a detail that the summary dropped …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good summary: the second shop opens in **Zarqa** next **Saturday** at
   **9:00**; it is open Saturday to Thursday, 9:00 to 20:00; the first
   **50** customers get a free bag. A summary always drops details, for
   example the free pen for children, or that the shop is closed on Friday.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which summary of the report is good?

   - [x] The second shop opens in Zarqa next Saturday at 9:00; it is open Saturday to Thursday, 9:00 to 20:00; the first 50 customers get a free bag.

     Why: Three main points, and every one is in the report.

   - [ ] Sunrise opens a new shop. It will be great. Everybody is welcome.

     Why: No facts from the report: a summary keeps the main points.

   - [ ] The second shop opens next Friday at 10:00.

     Why: The report says Saturday at 9:00, and the shop is closed on Friday.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.png" title="Word AI Lab: draft, sum up, rewrite, translate" >}}

2. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Sum up**. Compare the three points with the
   memo and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong part, and the right fact" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   "Shop staff pick up the price list at **3 pm**": the memo says **5 pm**.
   A summary can change a number, so you find it in the original.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="5 pm|5|5pm|5 p.m.|17:00|5:00 pm" hint="Find the price list in the memo, not in the summary."}
   The summary says: "Shop staff pick up the price list at 3 pm." What time
   does the memo say?

   Why: The memo says 5 pm. A summary can change a number, so you check each one in the original.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A new tone

**The idea:** AI can **rewrite** a text: the same facts in other words,
shorter, simpler or more polite. The **tone** fits the reader: formal for a
customer that you do not know, friendly for a friend. A rewrite changes the
words and the tone, never the facts: delete every new promise.

**Aim:** let the AI say the same facts in other words, and keep the facts.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant)**
:::

1. In the AI assistant, type: *Rewrite this in a polite, formal tone for a
   customer: "We do not have your size. Come back next week."* Read the
   rewrite. Did the AI add a promise or a new fact, for example a discount,
   a call or a date?

   {{< record "The new sentence … ; added (or: nothing) …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good rewrite: "Dear customer, we are sorry, but your size is not in
   the shop now. Please visit us again next week." If the AI added "We will
   call you" or "You get a 10 % discount", delete it: the shop did not
   promise it.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Keep or delete? Sort the sentences of a rewrite.

   Keep: the same facts
   :   Your size is not in the shop now.

       Why: The fact of the message, in polite words.

   :   Please visit us again next week.

       Why: "Come back next week", in polite words.

   :   We are sorry.

       Why: Polite words, no new fact.

   Delete: a new promise
   :   We will call you.

       Why: The shop did not promise a call.

   :   You get a 10 % discount.

       Why: The shop did not promise a discount.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/tone-lab.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/tone-lab.png" title="Tone Lab: one message in three tones" >}}

2. Do the three tasks of **Tone Lab**: choose the tone and the length for
   each reader.

   {{< record "Task 1 … ; Task 2 … ; Task 3 …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Task 1:** formal and short (a customer that you have never met).
   **Task 2:** friendly and short (a customer who is your friend).
   **Task 3:** formal and long (a letter for the company file).
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which tone and length fits each reader of Tone Lab? Sort them.

   Formal and short
   :   Mr Haddad, a big customer that you have never met

       Why: Formal for a person you do not know; short for an e-mail.

   Friendly and short
   :   Sami, a customer who is also your friend, in a chat

       Why: Friendly for a person you know well, in a chat.

   Formal and long
   :   a letter for the company file

       Why: A letter for the file needs all the facts, in a formal tone.
   :::

## Experiment 4 · A translation

**The idea:** AI and Word translate a short text in seconds (**Review ›
Translate**). A machine translation can change a day, a number or a name,
so you check each one before you use the text.

**Aim:** translate in Word, then check the days, times, numbers and names.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. In `report-start.docx`, select the second paragraph (*Sunrise Company
   opens its second shop …*). Choose **Review › Translate › Translate
   Selection** and the language **Arabic**. Check the day, the time and the
   names.

   {{< record "The day and the time in Arabic" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A right translation says **السبت** (Saturday) and **9:00** (الساعة
   التاسعة), and the names **الزرقاء** and **شارع الملك عبدالله**. No
   Translate in your Word? Use Word on the web.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which Arabic word is right for **Saturday**?

   - [x] السبت

     Why: السبت is Saturday.

   - [ ] الجمعة

     Why: الجمعة is Friday.

   - [ ] الأحد

     Why: الأحد is Sunday.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.png" title="Word AI Lab: draft, sum up, rewrite, translate" >}}

2. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Translate**. Compare the Arabic with the
   English memo and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong word, and the right one" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **الثلاثاء** is Tuesday, but the memo says Thursday: **الخميس**. A
   machine translation can change a day, so you check it.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The Arabic says الثلاثاء, but the memo says Thursday. Which word is right?

   - [x] الخميس

     Why: الخميس is Thursday; الثلاثاء is Tuesday. A machine translation can change a day.

   - [ ] الأربعاء

     Why: الأربعاء is Wednesday.

   - [ ] الثلاثاء

     Why: الثلاثاء is Tuesday: that is the mistake.
   :::
